title: Pin Confirmation Modal — Accessibility, Copy Variants & Edge Flows
content:
Purpose:
This note captures the UX and copy direction for the model-version pin confirmation modal, with a heavy focus on accessibility (keyboard + screen reader), microcopy variants for different user contexts, and edge-case/error flows. Aim is to provide a single reference for design, dev, and QA for the next sprint (rollout: canary to beta).

Problem statement / context:
- Current pin flows (existing wires) assume visually-oriented users and include minimal confirmation language. Support teams report confusion when a pin replaces active traffic routes (customers misinterpret what \"pin\" does).
- We need a compact confirmation modal that: clearly communicates impact, surfaces fallback behavior, supports keyboard-first users, provides explicit accessible text for screen readers, and includes copy variants for novice vs. power users.

Success criteria (what good looks like):
- 95% of test participants correctly state the impact of pinning after seeing the modal in unmoderated tests.
- Modal meets WCAG 2.1 AA guidelines for contrast and semantics; keyboard trap avoided; focus returned to originating control on close.
- No regressions in e2e rollout testing (JIRA-ROLL-1023).

Wireframe summary (compact modal):
- Header: "Pin model version to endpoint"
- Body copy (short): 2 lines max explaining impact and fallback.
- Primary CTA (left): "Confirm pin" (danger-low styling)
- Secondary CTA (right): "Cancel"
- Optional: a small link to "More about pinning" opens side panel or docs (non-blocking)
- Footer: subtle inline note with current active route and who last deployed (if available)

Keyboard / focus behavior (requirements):
- When modal opens, focus should land on the modal container role=dialog with aria-modal=true and on an H1 inside for screen readers.
- First tabbable element = cancel button, second = confirm. This reduces accidental confirmation when users are tabbing forward.
- Escape closes modal and returns focus to the original "Pin" button.
- When Confirm is activated, focus moves to an inline status toast with role=status (announce start of operation).

Screen reader text (explicit strings):
- Dialog aria-label: "Confirm pin model version"
- Hidden paragraph (aria-live polite) after confirm: "Pinning in progress. If the pin succeeds, requests to this endpoint will remain on the pinned model version until unpinned. If it fails, the endpoint will continue using its last stable route."
- Error announcement (aria-live assertive): "Pin failed: {short-error-message}. See details."

Copy variants (aim for short + explanatory):
- Variant A (compact, default):
  - Title: "Pin model version to endpoint"
  - Body: "Keep this endpoint on the selected model version. This will maintain responses on the pinned version until you unpin or change the route. Traffic will not be switched to other variants automatically."
  - Confirm: "Confirm pin"
  - Cancel: "Cancel"
  - Microlink: "Learn more about pinning"

- Variant B (novice, more explicit):
  - Title: "Lock endpoint to a specific model version"
  - Body: "Pinning prevents the endpoint from automatically switching models (for rollouts or fallback). If you pin now, some newer model improvements may not be used by this endpoint. You can unpin anytime to re-enable normal routing."
  - Confirm: "Pin and keep"
  - Cancel: "Not now"

- Variant C (power-user, terse):
  - Title: "Pin version"
  - Body: "Pin v{version} — route will remain on this build until unpinned. Fallback: automatic to configured fallbacks."
  - Confirm: "Pin v{version}"
  - Cancel: "Abort"

Tone and voice guidance:
- Use plain language, avoid jargon like "route lock" or "pin gating".
- Avoid fear language — preference for neutral facts and a single explicit action.
- When contextual info is present (who deployed, last changed), surface it in a muted inline row to help reviewers.

Error and edge flows:
- Confirm fails due to conflict (someone else changed route in parallel): show modal error state with body: "Pin couldn't complete because the endpoint route changed. Refresh to see current route or try again." Primary CTA becomes "Refresh" and secondary "Try again" which re-opens the modal after refresh check.
- Quota / permission error: "You don’t have permission to pin this endpoint. Contact your admin or use the audit log to request approval." CTA: "Open audit log" (links to logs).
- Long-running operation: if pin operation takes > 5s, show progress spinner + cancelable action. If > 20s, surface troubleshooting link and allow backgrounding the job (toast with link to activity page).

Accessibility checklist for QA (deliverable testable items):
- Dialog must have role=dialog and aria-modal=true; labelledby points to H1 inside.
- Focus trap implemented (no focus escape to behind screen).
- Tab order: Cancel -> Confirm -> More info -> Close (X) -> then out of dialog controls.
- All interactive elements keyboard reachable, actionable with Enter/Space.
- Contrast ratios for buttons and body text meet WCAG AA (test values: primary CTA on white background >= 4.5:1).
- Screen reader announces start/end of pin operation via polite/assertive live regions.

Localization notes:
- Keep title and CTAs short to avoid truncation in locales with long strings (de, ru, ja).
- Do not include embedded links inside body copy for translations; use a microlink after body for docs.
- Placeholder tokens: use explicit token format e.g., "v{version}" and avoid concatenation in translators.

Analytics / telemetry suggestions (for Product insights):
- Track: modal_opened, modal_confirmed, modal_cancelled, modal_error_{type}, modal_learn_link_clicked. Include metadata: endpoint_id, version, user_role, time_to_confirm_ms.
- Use events to drive educational nudges if high cancel rates on novice copies.

Backlog and open questions (prioritized):
- [P0] Behavior when endpoint has active traffic split: do we show additional blocker requiring confirmation of traffic move? (Unresolved: engineering needs input on transactional semantics) -> JIRA-ROLL-1023.
- [P1] Should we include a "Pin and create release note" checkbox for auditability? (SWE + Security input) -> add spike.
- [P1] Can we expose last successful healthcheck timestamp in the inline row? (UX + SRE feasibility).
- [P2] Microcopy A/B test for novice vs compact for new users (metric: successful comprehension).

QA test cases (quick list):
- Open modal via keyboard only, confirm, ensure focus and live regions announce progress.
- Simulate conflict error and check error message + CTA semantics.
- Permission-denied path: CTA opens audit log and breadcrumbs.
- Long-running op: cancel mid-operation and verify rollback/no partial pin.
- Localization: German strings do not overflow buttons (use test build).

Design assets / mockups references:
- See linked PR (console/pull/214) for Figma frames: frame names "Pin modal / default" and "Pin modal / error - conflict".

Notes for devs (implementation tips):
- Keep modal HTML minimal; rely on screen-reader-only paragraphs for longer explanations rather than cluttering visual design.
- Expose an API hook to report pin start/completion for telemetry and to show background job link.
- When possible, derive the blame (who last deployed) on server-side to avoid exposing extra requests from the client.

Next steps / owner actions:
- Jordan: iterate final microcopy and push updated strings to i18n catalog (due 2026-03-17).
- Evan: spike on transaction semantics for simultaneous route changes (due 2026-03-14).
- Priya: schedule unmoderated comprehension study for microcopy variants (target n=50, results by 2026-04-01).

Open feedback items (please comment inline):
- Are we comfortable with Confirm as left-side primary CTA? (we prefer Cancel-first tab stop to reduce accidental pin).
- Should the modal be dismissible via backdrop click in canary? (Security suggests explicit cancel only)

Anchors / reference links:
- Pinning concept doc: CONFLUENCE-REQS-789
- Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/214
- Rollout ticket: JIRA-ROLL-1023

End of note.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-03 initial draft (Priya)
- 2025-12-02 added a11y checklist (Jordan)
- 2026-03-10 updated dev notes + telemetry keys (Evan)
